erydon.name: ERYDON
erydon.overview: ERYDON is the Collection's detailed architectural building mod: stone and marble families, connected textures, slopes and structural pieces, lighting, and classical through Modern details.

practicalHelp.answer: Use ERYDON when you want detailed architectural building pieces and a shared material language across a structure. Start with the main shape and material, then choose details such as cornices, surrounds or lighting; an exact form/material combination should still be checked in the installed catalogue.

The inspected ERYDON build uses its own Synapheia connected-texture engine. Continuity is neither required nor bundled for that path, so missing CTM should first be investigated through the actual version, active resources and renderer setup rather than assuming Continuity must be added.

The source includes /erydon swap for changing supported materials and finishes while keeping the matching shape, including installed Daedalon and Themelios counterparts. It requires operator level 2; missing counterparts remain unchanged, so this is a scoped tool rather than a promise that every possible shape can be converted.

unknowns: Latest public release availability was not checked.
No ERYDON ports beyond the inspected Fabric1.20.1 target are implied.
A real installed registry is needed before promising an exact item or form/material combination.

daedalon.name: Daedalon
daedalon.overview: Daedalon is the standalone sculpture and detailed decoration part of the Collection, with freestanding OBJ ornaments and architectural decorative objects.

practicalHelp.answer: Daedalon's ordinary Creative search and optional item browsers share material, style and shape vocabulary. Try a form such as vase, bench, pedestal or column capital, then add a material or style clue; this is more useful than guessing an exact registry ID.

Identify the decoration first: its exposed debug-stick controls depend on the family. Reviewed benches, lanterns, panels and statues have useful local control notes, but an older statue's physical front or another mod's object must not be inferred from a generic facing rule.

Daedalon's inspected detailed models use a built-in world-aligned repeat renderer, without requiring Continuity. Fabric API supplies the normal renderer; the README says Sodium and Iris are optional and that Sodium0.5.x needs a compatible Indium release for this rendering path.

The documented fountain particle setting has Normal and High modes; High uses four times the liquid-drop and landing-ripple budget. Normal restores the original budget. It is a client setting, and Minecraft's particle settings still apply.

unknowns: The README still calls its native-texture checkpoint1.0.1 while gradle.properties is1.0.2; use the live property as source version, not a release assertion.
No real game session or shader integration was tested in this knowledge pass.

themelios.name: Themelios
themelios.overview: Themelios is a compact, standalone catalogue of basic architectural shapes using the Collection's material vocabulary. It is useful for building the main structure and smaller custom details, rather than being a required ERYDON add-on.

practicalHelp.answer: The inspected catalogue includes full blocks, slabs, stairs, walls, posts, horizontal and vertical slices and layers, cylinders and cornices. Use these simpler forms to establish structure or make small proportional adjustments, then add richer ornament where it matters.

For the inspected posts and layer blocks, placing the same item on an existing compatible piece can add another layer when the clicked face permits it. The source preserves the existing orientation and water state during a merge; the exact placement face depends on the shape family.

The inspected Themelios README uses native16x textures and supports the shared optional Collection32x/64x packs. Its built-in Synapheia engine does not require Continuity; for Sodium0.5.x the README calls for compatible Indium. These are version-scoped requirements, not a blanket instruction for every future renderer.
Themelios can be used as its own building set. Its inspected required dependencies are Fabric Loader, Fabric API, the matching Minecraft target and Java; ERYDON is not a required mod dependency.

unknowns: The separate1.21.1 source root was not audited in this pass; do not turn a repository link into a publication or compatibility claim.
Every form's full placement controls were not reviewed.

metrakron.name: Metrakron
metrakron.overview: Metrakron is an independent client loading timer. It measures startup and world-loading time, learns from recent completed loads and estimates the remaining wait; it does not make Minecraft load faster or increase FPS.

practicalHelp.answer: Metrakron uses its own clock and an average of the latest three completed loads, rather than reading Minecraft's progress percentage. A first or changed setup needs learning, and a load that runs longer than the estimate can show overtime instead of pretending it has finished.

With a matching optional Mod Menu, open Mods, choose ERYDON Metrakron and Configure. Its appearance screen offers stone, font, metal and position choices with Save, Cancel and Reset. The timer itself does not require Mod Menu.

The documented fallback cannot refresh while Minecraft itself is frozen when a desktop AWT window is unavailable, including the stated Wayland limitation. That does not establish the cause of any particular frozen overlay; collect the operating environment and exact symptom before diagnosing it.

unknowns: Publication availability of each adapter was not verified.
Pending desktop-renderer edits are not a tested or released remedy.
This timer is not a rendering-performance optimiser.

lithotheca.name: Lithotheca
lithotheca.overview: Lithotheca is a Creative block picker and extended hotbar for working with the blocks already supplied by installed mods. It helps find, compare and arrange building items; it is not another stone-block content set.

practicalHelp.answer: The inspected default opener is the remappable L key or the Creative plaque; L also closes the picker, and Ctrl+F focuses search. Match, Nearby, Browse and Hotbar views, with Shapes and Textures facets, help narrow the currently installed block catalogue.

Left-click a result to pick one block onto the cursor, then click or drag it into a hotbar slot to place or swap it. A click outside the hotbar discards that cursor selection. This is a Creative workflow, not a way to bypass Survival inventory rules.

The hotbar scrolls as one continuous bar. The source allows0–18 extra slots, default9; middle-click selects a matching stack or the first empty extra slot, and a full bar follows vanilla replacement behavior. For multiplayer extra storage, confirm the server has Lithotheca too.

Lithotheca shows blocks from currently installed sources, including ERYDON, Themelios, Daedalon and other block mods, and caches catalogues per source. Axiom and recipe-browser hooks exist, but the README leaves real gameplay compatibility checks open, so I would not promise every combination has been live-tested.

unknowns: Upcoming status is user-confirmed; launch date and public download are not established.
Axiom and recipe-browser hooks are not universal gameplay compatibility proof.

georgian.answer: For a Georgian-inspired direction, start with ordered proportions, regular openings and a clear main axis. Keep the decorative emphasis restrained so the overall arrangement remains easy to read.
georgian.boundary: Curated general design guidance, not a historical specification or proof of every registered Georgian form.

gothic.answer: For a Gothic-inspired direction, use a stronger vertical rhythm and pointed forms, balanced with quieter surfaces. Decide where the strongest detail belongs rather than making every surface equally elaborate.
gothic.boundary: General design guidance. Gothic and Gothic Ornate are distinct Collection family names.

byzantine.answer: For a Byzantine-inspired direction, organise rich repeated pattern around a clear centre or axis and a disciplined material palette. Begin with one readable pattern before layering in more ornament.
byzantine.boundary: General design guidance. Byzantine architecture naming does not rename Guilloche metal-inlay motifs.

modern.answer: Modern is the Collection's approved style name. Use clear proportions, clean planes and restrained ornament, allowing material and the main volumes to do more of the work.
modern.boundary: Do not rename Modern to Stripped Classical.

gothic_ornate.answer: In the Collection, Gothic Ornate Surround is a specific ornate family. It is not an alias for the separate plain Gothic family, so exact names matter when finding a matching piece.

materialGuidance.answer: For a pale main surface with a dark accent, Glacium and Nerium are a grounded starting pair in the inspected ERYDON source. Glacium's native artwork is pale and Nerium's is dark with light veining; try a small sample under the active pack and lighting before committing. Imperium offers a darker brown direction. These are verified material names, not a promise that every requested shape exists in each finish.

paletteSuggestions.answer: Test mostly Glacium with a limited Nerium accent, keeping the main field calm and repeating the accent deliberately.
paletteSuggestions.kind: Design suggestion using verified named materials

materialGuidance.boundary: Native artwork was visually checked. Active packs, shaders and lighting can change appearance; no RGB match or universal historical origin is claimed. Do not construct unverified shape IDs by substituting material prefixes.

vanilla.answer: Are you changing one block's state or rotating a whole selection? For an identified Daedalon block in the reviewed source, use its exposed debug-stick control; the relevant name can be Orientation or Facing, and Size or Width is separate. Debug-stick permission is required, and another block family may work differently.
vanilla.boundary: This is scoped Daedalon debug-stick guidance, not a claim that every vanilla block has one universal rotate control.

axiom.answer: In Axiom, distinguish moving the selection outline from transforming copied content. Copy or Duplicate the intended selection, then use the rotation rings available on that tool's active gizmo; X, Y and Z rings rotate around their respective axes. The available gizmo controls depend on the tool and mode.
axiom.boundary: Official documentation reviewed; no universal keyboard shortcut or arbitrary-angle support for every block is promised. Complete multi-part object selection still needs family-specific checks.

worldedit.answer: WorldEdit's //copy puts the selected region on the clipboard and remembers your position relative to it. //rotate 90 turns that clipboard around the vertical axis, then //paste places the result; rotating the clipboard does not itself turn the original placed build. The copy position matters for the pivot, so test the destination and required permissions before pasting.
worldedit.boundary: Scoped to official current clipboard documentation, not every installed version or every custom multi-block assembly. No commands are executed by Glaux.

clarify: Is the frame rate continuously low, or are there brief pauses?
Does it follow one view, a dense decorated area, or the whole world?
Which shader, render distance, active packs and rendering mods are in use?
firstChecks: Compare the same position and view before changing anything else; note the reported FPS or frame time.
In a separate test setup or under the player's control, compare one change at a time: fewer visible detailed objects, lower render distance, or the shader disabled, then restore the previous setting.
Distinguish client rendering FPS from delayed block interactions or server tick lag. Metrakron measures loading, not in-world FPS.
stopAndHandoffWhen: A specific mod conflict, driver issue or cause is being inferred without evidence.
The problem needs logs, a reproducible setup or a measured game profile.
fps.boundary: A hypothesis and controlled comparison are not a diagnosis. No game FPS result was measured in this knowledge pass.

clarify: When does the pause occur: startup, world entry, first view of an area, opening a menu, resource reload or at regular intervals?
Did it begin after a mod, pack, shader or setting changed?
Does the rest of the game keep responding?
firstChecks: Separate a cold first load from repeated steady play in the same view.
Record a short repeatable sequence and change one optional setting at a time in a test setup.
If the pause happens in an inventory or catalogue, identify that screen and whether the first opening differs from later openings.
stopAndHandoffWhen: Memory, garbage collection, chunk generation or shader compilation is being declared the cause without measurements.
stutter.boundary: Loading duration, frame pacing and server lag are different measurements.

clarify: Does the failure happen before the main menu, while loading a world, or during play?
What is the exact first useful error or dependency message?
What changed immediately before it started?
firstChecks: Compare the error's stated Minecraft, loader and dependency requirements with the actual installed JARs; do not apply one product's versions to all five.
Check for duplicate or wrong-target mod JARs without deleting anything automatically.
Keep the original error available and review sensitive text before sharing a selected log excerpt on the website.
stopAndHandoffWhen: A crash needs a complete stack trace, installed-mod inventory or reproduction.
The player would need risky file removal or a world conversion to continue.
crash.boundary: Do not recommend update-everything, arbitrary RAM increases or deleting caches/worlds as a universal cure.

clarify: Are ordinary full blocks affected, detailed custom models affected, or both?
Which packs are actually active and in what priority?
Is the issue missing geometry, missing connections, wrong texture, or metal/reflection appearance?
firstChecks: For the inspected ERYDON and Themelios builds, check built-in Synapheia and the active resource layers rather than assuming Continuity is required.
Compare a known ordinary block and the affected model under the same setup. A higher-priority pack can replace resources, so presence on disk is not proof that its assets are active.
Metallic colour alone does not reproduce the website's studio reflections; compare lighting and shader setup separately.
Use a controlled native-resource or optional-pack comparison only with the player's choice, preserving the existing configuration.
stopAndHandoffWhen: The active resource provider, model chain or exact renderer combination needs inspection.
The symptom requires screenshots, selected logs or a real game test.
visual.boundary: Do not resize or replace textures merely because a pack is named32x or64x. Third-party override packs are not automatically official Collection packs.

clarify: What are the exact Minecraft and loader targets?
Which versions are actually loaded on the client, and what is known about the server?
For the three block-content mods and official packs, what compatibility generation does their metadata report?
firstChecks: Match Minecraft and loader targets before comparing semantic versions.
The inspected ERYDON/Themelios/Daedalon family check requires matching numeric compatibility generations and rejects a missing generation; their semantic version numbers remain independent.
For official Collection packs, check asset generation, family generation, pack release and resolution separately. The pack release is not the family generation.
Do not assume the same block-family generation check applies to independent client utilities such as Metrakron or to Lithotheca; inspect their own metadata and role.
For Lithotheca multiplayer extra slots, confirm server installation rather than relying only on the client catalogue.
stopAndHandoffWhen: An exact public download, port or server compatibility claim has not been verified.
The error involves old-world identifiers or custom block-state migration.
compatibility.boundary: Loaded on this client, installed on a server and publicly released are separate facts.
